You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0205.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

content:
2026.03.1

AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure( (Mol)mol [, (int)confId=-1 [, (bool)replaceExistingTags=True]]) -> None :
    Sets the chiral tags on a molecule's atoms based on
      a 3D conformation.
      NOTE that this does not check to see if atoms are chiral centers (i.e. all
      substituents are different), it merely sets the chiral type flags based on the
      coordinates and atom ordering. Use AssignStereochemistryFrom3D() if you
      want chiral flags only on actual stereocenters.
    
      ARGUMENTS:
    
        - mol: the molecule to use
        - confId: the conformer id to use, -1 for the default 
        - replaceExistingTags: if True, existing stereochemistry information will be cleared
        before running the calculation.
    
    

    C++ signature :
        void AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(RDKit::ROMol {lvalue} [,int=-1 [,bool=True]])

cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
import numpy as np
els=['C','C','C','C','C','C','N','C','C','C','C','C','C','C','C','N','C','C','C','C','C','H','H']
edges=[(0,1,'AROMATIC'),(1,2,'AROMATIC'),(2,3,'AROMATIC'),(3,4,'AROMATIC'),(4,5,'AROMATIC'),(5,0,'AROMATIC'),(4,6,'SINGLE'),(6,7,'SINGLE'),(7,12,'SINGLE'),(12,3,'SINGLE'),(7,8,'SINGLE'),(8,9,'SINGLE'),(9,10,'SINGLE'),(10,11,'SINGLE'),(11,12,'SINGLE'),(12,13,'SINGLE'),(13,14,'SINGLE'),(14,15,'SINGLE'),(15,11,'SINGLE'),(15,16,'SINGLE'),(16,17,'SINGLE'),(17,18,'SINGLE'),(18,10,'SINGLE'),(10,19,'SINGLE'),(19,20,'SINGLE'),(7,21,'SINGLE'),(11,22,'SINGLE')]
xy=[(20,198),(92,101),(210,114),(261,225),(190,321),(70,309),(257,417),(374,383),(478,443),(582,383),(582,261),(478,200),(374,259),(293,142),(363,44),(478,80),(582,20),(686,80),(686,201),(648,298),(700,344),(374,465),(478,282)]
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for el in els: rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom(el))
for a,b,order in edges: rw.AddBond(a,b,getattr(Chem.BondType,order))
m=rw.GetMol(); Chem.SanitizeMol(m)
conf=Chem.Conformer(len(els))
for i,(x,y) in enumerate(xy):
    z= (-1 if i==21 else 1 if i in (22,19) else 0)
    conf.SetAtomPosition(i,(x/100,-y/100,z))
m.AddConformer(conf)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(m)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m, cleanIt=True,force=True)
print('Before adding hydrogen:',Chem.MolToSmiles(m))
for i in [7,10,11,12,19,21,22]:
 a=m.GetAtomWithIdx(i)
 print(i,a.GetChiralTag(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode') if a.HasProp('_CIPCode') else 'no CIP', [(n.GetIdx(),n.GetSymbol()) for n in a.GetNeighbors()])
m.RemoveAllConformers()
m=Chem.AddHs(m)
print('With H:',Chem.MolToSmiles(m))
par=AllChem.ETKDGv3(); par.randomSeed=71202; par.numThreads=0; par.maxIterations=400
par.pruneRmsThresh=0.15
ids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(m,numConfs=65,params=par)
print('Embedded',len(ids))
res=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(m,numThreads=0,maxIters=700)
scores=sorted((e,i,s) for i,(s,e) in enumerate(res))
print('scores',scores[:15])
for rank,(energy,i,status) in enumerate(scores[:5]):
 conf=m.GetConformer(i)
 xyz=f'candidate{rank}.xyz'
 with open(xyz,'w') as f:
  f.write(f'{m.GetNumAtoms()}\nMMFF E={energy:.3f} conf={i} status={status}\n')
  for atom in m.GetAtoms():
   pos=conf.GetAtomPosition(atom.GetIdx()); f.write(f'{atom.GetSymbol():2s} {pos.x: .8f} {pos.y: .8f} {pos.z: .8f}\n')
PY
python build.py

command -v xtb || true; head -n 8 candidate0.xyz; python - <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Geometry import Point3D
f='candidate0.xyz'
m=Chem.MolFromXYZFile(f)
print('atoms',m.GetNumAtoms())
PY

python - <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
exec(open('build.py').read().split('m.RemoveAllConformers()')[0])
for p in ('candidate0.xyz','candidate2.xyz','candidate3.xyz'):
 xyz=Chem.MolFromXYZFile(p); m.RemoveAllConformers(); m.AddConformer(xyz.GetConformer()); Chem.AssignStereochemistryFrom3D(m,replaceExistingTags=True)
 print(p, [(i,m.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode') if m.GetAtomWithIdx(i).HasProp('_CIPCode') else '?') for i in (7,10,11,12)])
PY
